_comment: Configuration for the 'event-modeling-agents-watch' scheduled task. Edit this file to change what the weekly watch looks for. The task reads it at the start of every run. Add/remove items freely; keep it valid JSON.
_scope_options: Each watch axis has its own scope. 'focus-only' = capture only items touching the listed topics (a narrow net for on-target material). 'anything-substantive' = capture any notable new post regardless of topic, flagging off-thread items in the report (used for the people watch, where the value is the author, not the keyword match). PER-TOPIC OVERRIDE: a topic may carry its own `scope` field, which TAKES PRECEDENCE over the global `topic_scope` for that topic. This lets the tight EM×agents intersection stay 'focus-only' while the broader design-substrate topics run 'anything-substantive'.
_social_topic_search: TOPIC-LEVEL SOCIAL SEARCH (added per Dannie 2026-07-08). In addition to the web `queries`, each topic may carry a `social_queries` object with `x` and `linkedin` term/hashtag lists. During a sweep, run these as keyword/hashtag searches ON the platform (X search + LinkedIn search), NOT as web searches — they surface topic discourse that never reaches a blog (the loop-engineering thread in particular lives on X first). A social hit inherits that topic's `scope` (focus-only topics keep only genuinely on-topic items; anything-substantive topics keep any notable hit and flag off-thread). This is DISTINCT from the people watch, which follows named authors; here the axis is the KEYWORD, so it catches new voices. CONSTRAINT: X/LinkedIn are login-walled + client-rendered, so these run ONLY in a LIVE logged-in Chrome session (Dannie is logged in) — navigate to the platform search URL, scroll, and collect post text+timestamps via javascript_tool (get_page_text alone returns too little); see `_x_coverage`. In a HEADLESS scheduled run, SKIP social_queries and note in the report that a live-Chrome sweep is needed to cover them (a plain web search for the same terms is a weak fallback, fine to run opportunistically). Dedupe social hits against raw/ and the people-watch finds so an author's post isn't filed twice. Social posts capture to raw/notes/.
_x_coverage: X/Twitter IS part of the people watch (STEP 2 says check each person's blog/linkedin/X). Like LinkedIn, X timelines are login-walled + client-rendered: headless WebFetch returns an empty shell and get_page_text grabs only the pinned tweet, so X posts otherwise enter the wiki only via incidental web-search hits. For a real X sweep, drive it in a LIVE logged-in Chrome session (Dannie is logged in): navigate to https://x.com/<handle>, then scroll + collect article text/timestamps via javascript_tool (get_page_text alone only returns the pinned tweet). Added per Dannie 2026-06-19. Per-person `x` handles are listed below; treat them with the same anything-substantive + flag-off-thread rule as LinkedIn. Observed 2026-06-19: adymitruk = off-thread World Cup reposts; vladikk = short AI-economy aphorisms (substance stays on his blog) — both quiet on-thread.

topics.name: Event Modeling × AI agents
topics.description: The intersection of AI agents / agentic systems and Event Modeling (Adam Dymitruk's design method) — not just event sourcing. Keep this net TIGHT: an item qualifies only if it connects agents/LLMs to Event Modeling specifically.
queries: discrete-event / formal specification of LLM agents

topics.name: Event Modeling (method-wide)
topics.description: Event Modeling as a design method in its OWN right — Adam Dymitruk's timeline-of-events approach (3 building blocks, 4 patterns, 7-step workshop, swimlanes, GWT-per-slice) — captured BROADLY, with or WITHOUT an AI-agents angle (added per Dannie 2026-07-03). This is the standalone complement to Topic-1 'Event Modeling × AI agents', which stays a TIGHT agent-intersection net; here, capture any substantive new Event Modeling material regardless of whether agents are involved: tutorials / worked examples, method extensions & debates, tooling (eventmodeling.org, eventmodelers.ai, Miro/Draw.io/Fraktalio boards, prooph board, qlerify), conference talks & recaps, comparisons with Event Storming / DDD, and applied case studies. FLAG items that ALSO connect to agents as extra-relevant (they likely belong under Topic-1 too). Prefer PRIMARY sources (eventmodeling.org, the method's own practitioners, conference recordings) over secondary how-tos; still dedupe against what Topic-1 and the people watch already surface so an on-agent EM post isn't filed twice.

topics.name: Event sourcing, DCB, CQRS, vertical slice architecture & business capabilities
topics.description: The design substrate around Event Modeling. Capture ANY substantive new development in these areas, with or without an AI-agents angle (per Dannie 2026-06-14). Flag items that DO connect to agents (extra-relevant) and note when an item is purely off the agents thread. Sub-areas: (1) event sourcing (event stores, projections, replay, aggregates); (2) Dynamic Consistency Boundaries / DCB — the 'kill the aggregate' line of work (Sara Pellegrini, Milan Savić et al.) on consistency boundaries decoupled from aggregates; (3) CQRS (command/query separation); (4) vertical slice architecture (feature slices over layered architecture; Jimmy Bogard lineage); (5) BUSINESS CAPABILITIES / capability-based design — capabilities as stable 'what-not-how' boundaries, capability maps, coupling/cohesion, business architecture, Wardley mapping of capabilities (FLAGGED IMPORTANT by Dannie 2026-06-14).
queries: "business capability" AND (bounded context OR capability map OR decomposition OR coupling)
capability-based design bounded context business architecture
business capability map Wardley event modeling

topics._revision_2026_08_31: REWORKED after outputs/topic-3-watch-diagnosis-2026-08-30.md. The old query set was eleven generic terms plus a year ("CQRS pattern 2026", "\"vertical slice architecture\" 2026"), which web search ranks by AUTHORITY not RECENCY — so they structurally could not surface a two-day-old post, and printed the same evergreen tier for fifteen consecutive sweeps. Fix: (a) name CHANNELS, the way Topics 1-2 already do; (b) keep only the few keyword queries that carry a discriminating term; (c) report the substrate BY THREAD, crediting whichever axis found it — see `reporting` below.

topics._queries_removed_2026_08_31: Dropped outright after fifteen sweeps produced nothing attributable to them: '"event sourcing" 2026 new', 'CQRS pattern 2026', '"vertical slice architecture" 2026', 'Jimmy Bogard vertical slice architecture' (he is now a `people` entry, which is the right axis for an author), 'event sourcing projections aggregates DCB talk'. The 'business capability' query gained a required architecture co-term because the bare phrase is a CONFIRMED HOMONYM TRAP — it returns corporate capability-maturity and consulting marketing, not architecture.
topics.reporting: REPORT THIS TOPIC BY THREAD, NOT BY AXIS. The old format reported the topic axis in isolation, so a week with three Fritzsche substrate captures still printed 'Topic-3: nothing new in window' — which is what produced the false impression of a dead field and triggered the 2026-08-30 diagnosis. Instead: gather every substrate capture from the run REGARDLESS of which axis found it (topic query, channel poll, or people watch), report them together under this topic, and credit the axis in parentheses. Only say 'nothing new' when NO substrate material was captured by ANY axis.
